cells.tense: Right now you're the steady hand in the pair, and being that isn't costing you much.
cells.ask: Give one growing thing an extra ten quiet minutes today that nobody asked for, then notice whether that was appreciation or just appetite.
cells.core:
Two things want your attention at once and neither gets dropped or smothered. You give the smaller one room, let the bigger one keep going on its own, and the arrangement holds without you gripping it. Nothing about this looks dramatic from the outside, which is part of why it works — the days go by and both things get what they need. That's a pair of hands in a good place, and it's yours.

What this steadiness can carry next is the receiving side: somebody noticing what you've been holding, and you letting that land instead of waving it off. Those ten minutes say something about which way you're leaning, and you get to keep whatever they say.

cells.tense: Part of you is already a few months out, standing where this has finally turned out right.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing you'd save if everything else went untended for a week, and let the rest go until next Monday on purpose.
cells.core:
There's a good version of this where each thing gets the time it actually takes and you can tell a sprout from something ready to stand. What's happening instead is a shoot half an inch out of the soil getting treated like it should be shoulder-high. So it gets more water and more arranging than any young thing can use, and the checking has its own momentum now — you're ahead of it, fixing what hasn't gone wrong yet.

Letting something take the time it takes is where the rest starts. Choosing one thing is the experiment, and it's not about which one deserves it most. It's about what happens to the others once you stop holding all of them at once.

cells.tense: Somewhere along the way you stepped back from tending much of anything, and you're still standing there.
cells.ask: Water one thing you've been leaving alone, and don't check afterward whether it looks any better.
cells.core:
Done the way it can go, this is unglamorous and steady — you keep an eye on what's coming up, give it what it needs, and it doesn't wipe you out. Lately those conditions aren't in place, and what needs tending is drifting. Everything reads as quietly closing up for the season, though nobody decided that.

The way back doesn't start with picking it all up at once; one thing, small enough to finish, is the whole ask. If it turns out you don't want to, that's worth knowing too, and it's yours.

cells.tense: The work is already happening under your hands; it's the claiming of it that's stalled.
cells.ask: Tell one person what you kept alive in the last month — plainly, without the shrug that follows it.
cells.core:
Quiet and ordinary when it's running well: arranging, checking, catching what's slipping before it slips. The effect lands on whoever's on the other end of it, day after day, and mostly goes unmentioned. What's missing is you saying so even in passing. It gets filed under circumstances or under somebody else's effort, and stays unnamed.

Saying it once is how it stops being absorbed. Do it to one person and let that be the end of it. No closing joke, no tribute to anyone else, and no taking it back.
